items.title: Bulls’ Norman Powell Suffers ‘Mild’ Right Hamstring Strain
items.summary: Bulls guard Norman Powell suffered a “mild” right hamstring strain during Friday’s NBA Cup loss to Washington and will be reevaluated later this week, the team announced (via Twitter). The update on Powell is pretty vague, and hamstring are notoriously tricky, but it’s noteworthy that the team used “mild” to describe the strain, tweets K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network. Johnson expects the Bulls to give a more definitive return timeline for Powell after he’s reexamined. The 46th overall pick in the 2015 draft, Powell made his first All-Star appearance last season with Miami and was Chicago’s main free agent signing over the summer. The veteran shooting guard has been the Bulls’ leading scorer early on this season, averaging 20.8 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 1.4 steals on .448/.341/.767 shooting splits through 13 games (29.5 minutes per contest). items.summary: Major injuries have largely defined the Thunder’s season to this point, but superstar guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander views the adversity as another way to improve his game, writes Chris Mannix of Sports Illustrated. “Since I’ve been this good, yeah, for sure,” Gilgeous-Alexander replied when Mannix asked if this was the most challenging season of his career. “But yeah, honestly speaking, it’s kind of fun. items.summary: The Sixers are tied for the NBA’s best record at 14-3, but they still aren’t finishing off opponents the way an elite team should, writes Kris Rhim of ESPN. The latest example came on Saturday afternoon against the one-win Bucks, as Philadelphia nearly squandered a 10-point lead with a little more than two minutes remaining. The game would have gone to overtime, but Tyler Herro’s three-pointer was ruled to have come a split-second after the final buzzer (Twitter video link). “Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better,” LeBron James said. “But a team like that, we know they’re scrappy. They’re going to play as hard as they can for their minutes. It’s about just getting the win, but we can learn from a lot of things that we didn’t do well tonight.” The Sixers improved to 12-0 in clutch games, but they’ve rarely been able to pull away from their opponents. items.title: Rockets Notes: Udoka, Defense, Sengun, Durant, VanVleet
items.summary: Rockets head coach Ime Udoka didn’t hide his disgust for his team’s effort following Friday’s NBA Cup loss in Denver, according to Varun Shankar of The Houston Chronicle. Udoka called the Rockets “mentally fragile” and was particularly critical of the defense, saying it lacked physicality, effort and “attention to detail.” In a back-and-forth contest with 32 lead changes and 17 ties, Houston was up five points with 5:10 remaining but was outscored 23-9 to close out the game. “You got to compete on (the defensive) end to give yourself a chance. You score 124, you should be able to win,” Udoka said. “But just count out the quarters. They had four 30-point quarters… you’re not going to win anything and that just shows a lack of effort, attention to detail or fight on that end. And so, doesn’t really matter what we did offensively. Play that poorly, you’re not going to win any games.”…
